workload: Standard maintained boot and exec/teardown using the same four exec windows. Compare normal/debug QEMU and RPi5 object/ELF sections, named storage, reservation starts and LLVM static frames against published 52d4017b. Measure compiler process cost separately with three sequential source-identical baseline/candidate pairs per target.
assessment: Accept static direct-call inference without maintained kernel/native annotation or runtime source changes. All allocated bytes/addresses, named storage, reservation starts and static frames are identical in four images. Normal artifacts match whole hashes; debug artifacts match after stripping working-directory DWARF. No pool, capacity, retained-page or occupancy benefit is claimed. Measured compile-time median growth is about 0.8/1.2 percent and allocation about 2.3 percent, within the unchanged compiler budget.
next_trigger: A new reference/storage shape requiring a materially different inference domain, a changed kernel allocation/reclamation workload, or completion of the next memory-safety consumer.
